div.head: Hn 5.27
div.ab: Gregorius in decretis: Presbiter uel diaconus uel quilibet clericus a populo accusatus, si certi non fuerint testes, illati criminis qui approbent ueritatem, iusiurandum sit in medio, et Illum proferant testem de innocencie sue puritate, cui nuda et aperta sunt omnia.

note.seg: Gr. C. 2 q. 5 c. 5. Er, Burchard und Ivo (Decr. VI 231; Pan. V 9) citiren Gregor [II] aus dessen Brief bei Jaffé-Löwenfeld Reg. Rom. n. 2174
Gr. C. 2 q. 5 c. 5. He, Burchard and Ivo (Decr. VI 231; Pan. V 9) cite Gregory [II] from his letter in Jaffé-Löwenfeld Reg. Rom. no. 2174
quil. sacerdos statt d. u. q. c. Gregor
quil. sacerdos instead of d. u. q. c. Gregory
so Gregor; dicant Burchard, Anselm, Ivo, Gratian
so Gregory; dicant Burchard, Anselm, Ivo, Gratian
uer. iureiurando, erit in m. Gregor; Sinn schon in einer Hs. und bei den Decretisten geändert
uer. iureiurando, erit in m. Gregory; the sense already altered in one MS and by the Decretists
uel quilibet fügt zu, aber vom Corr. unterpunctirt Sc
uel quilibet added, but expunged by the corrector, Sc
si fuerit ergänzt [unnöthig] Thorpe aus Gregor
si fuerit supplied [unnecessarily] by Thorpe from Gregory

Aus diesem Zitat schloss man früher, Verf. wolle hiermit Gratian anführen. Schon Somner (bei Wilkins Leg. Anglosax. 239) bemerkte dagegen, Lanfranc (Epist. ad Herbert. ed. 1648 p. 313) zitiere Bonifaz III in decretis. Später verweist Henr. Huntingdon. (III 5 ed. Arnold p. 69) für Augustin und Gregor I. auf decreta, womit er Gratian nicht meinen kann

It was formerly concluded from this citation that the author meant to cite Gratian here. Somner (in Wilkins Leg. Anglosax. 239), however, already objected that Lanfranc (Epist. ad Herbert. ed. 1648 p. 313) cites Boniface III in decretis. Later Henr. Huntingdon. (III 5 ed. Arnold p. 69) refers, for Augustine and Gregory I, to decreta, by which he cannot mean Gratian
